question: How many seats will the Republican Party win in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections?

forecast.reasoning: We anchor on the historical base rate of midterm seat losses for the president's party. With Republican Donald Trump in the White House, the Republican Party (holding a narrow 220-215 majority from 2024) is highly likely to lose seats. Current generic ballot polling averages from late August/early September 2026 show Democrats leading by about 6.5 to 6.6 percentage points. Historically, a generic ballot lead of this size translates to a Democratic majority, placing the most likely Republican seat count in the 200-217 range. We distribute the probabilities to reflect this, centering on 200-209 (35%) and 210-217 (30%), while leaving reasonable probability for a stronger Democratic wave (190-199 at 15%) or a polling error/Republican overperformance (218-225 at 12%).
key_drivers: Presidential midterm penalty (Republican President Donald Trump in office)
Narrow initial Republican majority (220-215) from the 2024 elections
Strong Democratic lead in generic congressional ballot polls (approx. D+6.6 as of late August/early September 2026)
